I checked every claim in the document against the record. All of them are supported, and I'm raising no flags.

- **Root cause and plain-words cause:** both rest on F1. The document says outright that F1 is a reading of the source that nothing ran, and uses "likely" in the plain-words version. So neither claims more than the record holds.
- **Before the onset:** the claim that the only failures logged were from shoppers closing the connection holds. G46bc covers 11:51–12:20, and the division-by-zero errors (G5309) start at 12:21.
- **Flag evaluations:** the claim that they went from all off to all on from that minute holds, though it's the closest call. In the 12:21 minute itself the split was 101 off and 99 on (G971b). That fits a single switch at 12:21:31 rather than a staged rollout, so I didn't flag it.
- **The other flag ruled out:** an-unrelated-feature was switched on at 12:27:18, after the errors began at 12:21. Only monthly-spend-feature was reverted, and the service recovered with the other flag still on.
- **Contributing factors:** "no check was seen" and "no staged rollout was seen" hold, because the record contains neither.
- **Went wrong:** "nobody was paged" is a finding the record names as one of its own. It isn't something the field rules out.

The action items and the "had it been otherwise" sentences aren't judged.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the call raises ZeroDivisionError. The error boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py then turns it into a failed account page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Someone switched on a setting that sent account pages through new monthly-spending code, and that code likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their pages failed.
Switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py.
Before the onset, the logs read show failures only from shoppers closing the connection.
That code started running on account page requests when admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}.
From that minute, the flag's evaluations went from all off to all on.
The feature flag an-unrelated-feature, which admin switched on at {P2.1}. The errors had already begun at the onset, before this change.
Switching only monthly-spend-feature off brought the service back while an-unrelated-feature stayed on.
With the flag on, account pages reached a monthly spend-per-item calculation that fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper with no purchases this month.
The flag went from off to on for all of the service's evaluations at once. No staged rollout was seen.
